Base cm/360° · calibrated to screenshots at 7 and 100

The H/V settings use a fixed 16:9 reference. Neither changes when you select a different resolution. The camera keeps the vertical FOV and expands the actual horizontal FOV on ultrawide displays without stretching the image. Optical zoom divides tan(FOV/2), not the angle in degrees.

The coefficient is measured relative to half the image height: 100% equals that distance from the center. The horizontal edge corresponds to 100 × width/height. 0% matches infinitesimal movements around the crosshair.

With USA disabled, the angular sensitivity multiplier is 1 (constant cm/360°). This is a geometric comparison, not an exact recreation of a game's legacy aiming mode. Sensitivity ranges from 0 to 200, with 7 as the default. At 7, the reference is 79 cm/360° at 800 DPI, 39.5 cm at 1600 DPI, and 19.8 cm at 3200 DPI. The affine model retains a small turning speed at 0. At 100, it gives 6.5 / 3.2 / 1.6 cm at 800 / 1600 / 3200 DPI, matching the reference screenshots. It agrees with a community measurement and is not an officially verified game formula. Raw mouse input is requested; browser or operating system scaling may affect physical distances.

Hold the right mouse button to aim; release it to return to hip fire. This works with or without mouse capture. While captured, left-click to shoot and use WASD to move. Only the body and head count as hits; the head counts as a headshot. A hit removes the target until its respawn delay expires, even when target movement is paused. Set the delay in Movement (5 s by default). New trials restore all targets. Accuracy is hits/shots, and the headshot percentage is headshots/hits. The ↺ button resets the counters. Hits and headshots have distinct sounds; misses are silent. A brief white hitmarker marks a body hit; red marks a headshot. Misses show no marker.

Space starts or stops mouse capture. Scroll up to increase zoom and down to decrease it in 0.25× steps, from 1× to 8×. Start or Space captures the mouse; Stop, Space, or Esc releases it. Numeric fields allow precise adjustments. Settings are saved automatically in this browser and restored when you return; statistics are not saved.

Start trial resets the statistics and starts the timer after mouse capture succeeds. Duration ranges from 0 to 300 seconds, with 60 as the default; 0 is unlimited. Time keeps running when the mouse is released. Scoring: +100 per hit, +50 extra per headshot, −25 per miss, with a minimum score of 0. When time expires, the result is frozen. To end an unlimited trial, press Esc and click Finish trial.
